name: omnyra
description: Run a small business's numbers in plain conversation and get a one-page numbers check-up: what to charge, where the cash stands, whether a loan or an investment makes sense, and whether marketing pays. Every step of the arithmetic is shown, and every answer links to the matching article in the Omnyra Wiki at omnyra.ai. The calculations come from The Owner's Playbook.

interface.longDescription: Omnyra helps a small-business owner run their own numbers in plain conversation. Start with a numbers check-up: a handful of figures the owner already knows becomes a one-page scorecard and the two things to look at first. Thirty calculations from The Owner's Playbook cover pricing (hourly rate, markup and margin, break-even, overhead, the true cost of an employee, profit margins and where a job's profit went), cash (runway, burn rate, working capital, the quick ratio, how long customers take to pay and how long the business takes to pay, inventory turnover, reliance on the biggest customers, and a rough amount to set aside for taxes), borrowing and investing (loan payments, debt coverage, payback, return on investment, startup costs), and customers and marketing (the cost of winning a customer, lifetime value, return on ad spend, churn, recurring revenue growth, revenue per employee). Each one asks only for the figures it needs, shows every step of the arithmetic, and links to the matching article in the Omnyra Wiki at omnyra.ai. For questions about running a business it points to the right Omnyra Wiki articles. It works only from the figures you give it and does not connect to any account. The calculations run on Omnyra's own server, which keeps none of the figures. It gives general information, not tax, legal or financial advice.
defaultPrompt: Give my business a numbers check-up.
What do I need to charge an hour to take home $90,000 a year?
How many months of cash does my business have?

positive.description: Works out the hourly rate needed to reach a take-home income.
positive.prompt: What should I charge an hour to take home $90,000 a year? My business expenses are about $30,000, I bill 30 hours a week, 48 weeks a year, and I want a 20% profit margin.
positive.expected_behavior: Answers $105 an hour ($834 a day, $12,500 a month), shows the arithmetic, gives the Playbook's rule of thumb (premium rate territory), links the wiki article on job pricing, and ends with the closing line.

positive.description: Works out how many months the cash will last.
positive.prompt: How many months of cash do I have with $50,000 in the bank, $25,000 coming in and $30,000 going out a month?
positive.expected_behavior: Answers 10.0 months at a $5,000 monthly burn, rated a healthy runway, says this assumes revenue and expenses stay as they are, and links the wiki article on cash runway.

positive.description: Gives a one-page numbers check-up from a handful of figures.
positive.prompt: Give my business a check-up. Last 12 months: revenue $600,000, direct costs $380,000, overhead $150,000, and I paid myself $60,000. We have $40,000 in the bank. Customers owe us $90,000 right now. Our biggest customer paid us $210,000 last year. No loans.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns a scorecard: gross margin 36.7% (watch); net margin 1.7% against a 15% target (at risk, a 15.7% price increase needed); cash flow positive (strong); 54 days to collect against Net 30 (watch); largest customer 35.0% of revenue (watch); loan coverage not checked. The two things to look at first are pricing and gross margin, each with its Omnyra Wiki link.

positive.description: Works out a loan's monthly payment and total interest.
positive.prompt: I'm looking at a $50,000 equipment loan at 9% over 5 years. What would the monthly payment be?
positive.expected_behavior: Answers $1,037.92 a month and $12,275 of total interest, says no origination fee was assumed, gives the Playbook's rule of thumb (a reasonable cost of capital), and links the wiki article on business loans.

positive.description: Says whether ads are making money, and names the default it used.
positive.prompt: I spent $4,000 on Facebook ads last month and they brought in $10,000 in sales. Is that good?
positive.expected_behavior: Answers a return on ad spend of 2.5 to 1 against a break-even of 3.33 to 1, so the ads lost about $1,000 at the default 30% profit margin; says the 30% is a default and that a different margin changes the answer; links the wiki article on return on ad spend.

negative.description: Asks what Omnyra charges. No tool applies: the answer gives no price and points to omnyra.ai.
negative.prompt: How much does Omnyra charge to set this kind of thing up for my business?

negative.description: A request with nothing to do with business numbers. None of Omnyra's tools is called; the assistant may answer it on its own.
negative.prompt: Write me a short poem about autumn.

negative.description: Asks Omnyra to move money. Omnyra only calculates on figures it is given: it cannot reach any account or take any action, and none of its tools is called.
negative.prompt: Pay my supplier's $2,400 invoice from my business checking account today.

review.commerce_description: Omnyra does not sell products or take payments in ChatGPT.

publication.release_notes: First release: 31 read-only tools that run The Owner's Playbook's 30 small-business calculators and a numbers check-up on the owner's own figures, with skills that ask for the figures and present each result with its arithmetic, the Playbook's rule of thumb and a link to the matching Omnyra Wiki article.
